Citation: Lee et al. (2026), Stamp removal from real documents: A diffusion-based approach with EA-RMSE evaluation
Dataset: physically stamped real documents + synthetic and virtual-document data
Main idea: Combines physically stamped and synthetic data and separates residual-stamp error from accidentally missing content.
Weakness: Targets general document content rather than forensic signature evidence; dataset is available by request.
Possible experiment: Adapt EA-RMSE to report lost signature evidence separately across occlusion levels.
Access status: open access; publisher requires interactive download

Citation: Hafemann, Sabourin & Oliveira (2017), Learning features for offline handwritten signature verification using deep convolutional neural networks
Architecture: deep CNN feature extractor with WI feature learning and downstream WD classifiers
Best result: 1.72% EER on GPDS-160 under the reported protocol
Main idea: Learns transferable signature representations from development writers and evaluates on disjoint writers.
Weakness: No stamp or occlusion setting; older CNN baseline and protocol choices must not be compared blindly with newer work.
Possible experiment: Use the representation as a clean baseline and measure degradation under controlled stamp occlusion.

Citation: Xiao & Wu (2025), Learning features for offline handwritten signature verification using spatial transformer network
Dataset: multilingual public signature datasets plus a Chinese forensic dataset; verify exact subsets
Architecture: two-stage Siamese CNN with spatial transformer network
Loss: focal loss plus pairwise objectives; verify details
Main idea: Uses spatial transformation to focus feature learning on discriminative handwriting regions and a Siamese-style comparison pipeline.
Weakness: No explicit occlusion model; strong preprocessing may remove information relevant to same-color stamp overlap.
Possible experiment: Test whether an explicit occlusion mask improves or destabilizes the learned attention under matched and mismatched stamp colors.

Citation: Zheng et al. (2025), HTCSigNet: A Hybrid Transformer and Convolution Signature Network for offline signature verification
Task: WD and WI offline signature verification
Architecture: parallel hybrid ViT and composite CNN blocks
Metrics: EER; AUC; FAR; FRR; dataset-specific metrics
Main idea: Combines global shape and layout with local stroke and micro-deformation features.
Weakness: No explicit stamp occlusion; full text requires publisher or institutional access.
Possible experiment: Compare hybrid features with a pure CNN verifier across occlusion severity and visible-stroke area.

Citation: Cui, Yang & Guo (2024), Generative adversarial networks for rubber stamp extraction and removal
Architecture: SERGAN double-cycle GAN with color-sensitive attention
Loss: cycle-consistency and image-translation objectives; verify details
Metrics: image restoration and extraction metrics; verify exact set
Main idea: Jointly extracts the stamp and generates an unstamped document using stronger cycle consistency.
Weakness: Generative restoration can hallucinate or destroy forensic strokes; LRSD is not publicly available.
Possible experiment: Use SERGAN-style restoration as Paradigm A and score lost signature pixels separately from visual quality.

Citation: Cui & Yang (2024), An enhanced diffusion-based network for efficient stamp removal
Architecture: diffusion model with spatial attention and SReLU
Best result: PSNR 44.7; SSIM 0.99; RMSE 3.47 on the reported stamp dataset
Main idea: Adds spatial attention and a custom activation to diffusion-based stamp removal.
Weakness: Primarily optimizes document appearance metrics that may miss destroyed forensic signature evidence.
Possible experiment: Re-evaluate outputs with EA-RMSE-style lost-evidence measures and downstream verification rather than PSNR alone.
Access status: publisher / institutional access; code linked by publisher
